name: codex
specialty: Strong at self-contained implementation and independent second-opinion review.
notes: Run codex exec with stdin from /dev/null (`codex exec <prompt> < /dev/null`); otherwise it waits on "Reading additional input from stdin". roster.py command returns this as stdin.

Model ids taken from `codex`'s model list on a ChatGPT Pro login on 2026-11-03: frontier gpt-6-astra, standard gpt-6.1-sol, economy gpt-6-luna. gpt-6.1-sol is the config.toml default, so an unpinned run (no -m) is the standard tier. Re-check ~/.codex/models_cache.json on that login and change these ids only when that list no longer contains them.

Reasoning effort is passed as `-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>` (`codex exec` config override) so it wins over a global model_reasoning_effort in ~/.codex/config.toml. Defaults are frontier high, standard medium, economy low. Builders stay within low, medium, and high. Sign-off may use xhigh when the seat scale asks for more than high. max and ultra are not chosen automatically (gpt-6-luna has no ultra) and are used only when explicitly requested.

codex exec defaults to a read-only sandbox, so builders pass --sandbox workspace-write rather than relying on the user config. Even then its sandbox cannot write the git index. Tell codex builders "do not commit"; the lead commits their work.
{prompt} is a fixed pointer to the prompt file, placed after -- so it is never read as a flag; the second-opinion seat runs --sandbox read-only.
